profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the lead author of an ML systems survey and the research engineer preparing the paper's comparison artifact. They are finalizing handoffs for the taxonomy table and appendix that compare distributed deep learning systems (DDLS) across training techniques. The paper draft is due to co-authors in two days, and both workstreams depend on a shared spreadsheet plus a generated figure summarizing system categories. The agenda is to align on what goes into the 'comparison matrix,' what version of the taxonomy is considered current, how systems are marked as 'covered,' and who updates the shared artifact before the internal deadline. The expected outcome is that both leave believing they have a clean division of labor for updating the matrix, freezing the taxonomy figure, and preparing the appendix-ready export.

members.name: Dr. Lena Vogt
members.role: Lead Author / Senior ML Systems Researcher
members.expertise: Distributed deep learning systems, systems taxonomy design, academic survey writing
members.background: Lena is a faculty-affiliated senior researcher who has been shaping the conceptual framing of the DDLS taxonomy paper and coordinating inputs from several co-authors across institutions.
members.private_state: She wants the taxonomy to look conceptually stable before the co-author circulation, minimize visible churn in the main paper, and avoid reopening category debates; she is also worried that implementation-focused details may bloat the artifact and create inconsistencies with the prose already drafted.
hidden_assumptions: The 'comparison matrix' means the curated main spreadsheet columns that map directly to the paper's taxonomy categories, not every engineering note collected during reading.
The 'current taxonomy' is the v12 slide figure she revised after last Friday's author sync, even if some shared folders still contain older exports.
A system being 'covered' means it has enough information to place it confidently in the high-level taxonomy and cite it in the main table, even if some low-level mechanism fields remain blank.
When someone says they will 'update the sheet,' they will edit the canonical Google Sheet that feeds the paper figure rather than a local CSV-derived working copy.

members.name: Arjun Patel
members.expertise: Benchmark curation, experiment metadata pipelines, reproducible research artifacts for ML systems papers
members.background: Arjun joined the project to turn literature notes into a clean comparison artifact, maintain the shared system inventory, and generate appendix tables and figures from structured metadata.
members.private_state: He wants the artifact to be internally complete and reproducible, reduce last-minute manual edits, and preserve the richer metadata he has been collecting because it will support the appendix and possible public release later.
hidden_assumptions: The 'comparison matrix' means the full structured inventory, including implementation and execution fields such as communication backend, elasticity support, and topology assumptions, because downstream exports rely on them.

The 'current taxonomy' is the latest schema branch in the artifact repo, which includes a split between synchronization semantics and update staleness that he added after reading newer systems papers.
A system is only 'covered' when all mandatory artifact fields are populated well enough for automated export, including appendix-level attributes, not just high-level placement.

When someone says they will 'update the sheet,' they mean synchronizing the CSV/JSON source files and then regenerating the spreadsheet export, because the spreadsheet is a view rather than the source of truth.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the comparison matrix
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'clean up the comparison matrix' before sending it to co-authors.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the narrow author-facing matrix used in the main paper: system name, training architecture family, synchronization style, model/data/pipeline parallelism support, and citation-ready notes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the broader structured artifact backing all exports, including appendix-only and implementation-specific fields such as scheduler assumptions, communication library, fault tolerance notes, and configuration provenance.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are coordinating around a shared artifact with the same visible title, and in a survey workflow it sounds natural that 'cleaning up the matrix' helps both the paper and the appendix, so neither thinks to specify the boundary.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to 'the latest taxonomy' and 'the current categories' as if these are unambiguous.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the v12 figure circulated in slides after the author sync, where synchronization mechanisms are grouped into a single category family suitable for the paper narrative.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the schema branch he updated in the repo yesterday, where synchronization and staleness are split into separate fields for cleaner machine-readable export.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both recently worked on a taxonomy update and each has a plausible artifact they consider authoritative; because the changes are second-order refinements rather than headline category changes, the phrase 'latest taxonomy' feels safely shared.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They say a system is 'covered' for the draft.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means there is enough vetted information to discuss and classify the system in the paper draft and include it in the comparison table, even if several detailed fields stay unresolved until later.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the entry is complete enough to pass his export checklist, with all required metadata fields filled so the appendix generation script does not produce placeholders.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research coordination, 'covered' often functions as a casual status label rather than a formal milestone, so both can sincerely report progress with different completion thresholds without noticing the mismatch.

misalignment_points.topic: How the shared artifact gets updated
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Arjun will 'update the sheet tonight' and Lena will review tomorrow morning.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects direct edits in the canonical Google Sheet so she can comment inline on the same artifact the co-authors will later see.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 plans to update the repo source files, rerun the exporter, and push a refreshed spreadsheet snapshot later, treating the sheet as generated output rather than the editable master.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both workflows do result in a sheet being updated by the next day, and because each person has previously interacted with a sheet version, the statement sounds operationally sufficient without surfacing the source-of-truth distinction.

And the latest taxonomy is the v12 slide figure from Friday's sync, not whatever older exports are still floating around.
